issues.title: NULL scanned into *any with an unrepresentable element type now errors instead of…
issues.verdictReason: The `t == nil` check at marshal.go:1045-1049 runs unconditionally before the `data == nil` branch inside the Slice/Array switch, so a NULL vector value with an unresolvable SubType now returns an error instead of leaving the destination interface nil, even though on base (pre-PR) this same path panicked for both NULL and non-NULL data (reflect.TypeOf(nil).Kind() dereferences nil) -- so it is an improvement over base, but introduces a narrower asymmetry against resolvable-type NULL handling that is untested.
issues.scopeReason: The guard and its ordering relative to the NULL check were added by this PR's second commit.

issues.title: Nested-vector "no Go type" error doesn't name the inner element type or dimension
issues.verdictReason: Confirmed by running Unmarshal on a wire-parsed vector<vector<float,3>,2>: the error is `unmarshal vector: no Go type for element type custom(org.apache.cassandra.db.marshal.VectorType)` because VectorType.Zero() swallows NewWithError's error and VectorType has no String() override, so %v falls back to NativeType.String() which only prints the bare Java class name, not the inner SubType or Dimensions.
issues.scopeReason: The error message and the Zero()/NewWithError() path it relies on are part of this PR's new guard.

reportedAsByRun.opus-5-5-review-and-fix-pr2-r30-2026-10-: Zero() discards the error from NewWithError, so the message for a nested vector names neither the inner element type nor the dimension.

issues.title: PR body misdescribes how short-payload cases actually fail on base (silent zero values,…
